entries.name: Install Claude Code
entries.description: Anthropic's official native installer for macOS, Linux and WSL, then print the version to confirm.
entries.author: voltius

snippets.name: Install Claude Code
snippets.description: Installs to ~/.local/bin and self-updates in the background.

steps.content:
curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash

# The installer adds ~/.local/bin to PATH in your shell profile; this session
# may not have picked it up yet.
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
claude --version

entries.name: What is filling the disk
entries.description: Filesystem usage, then the 20 largest directories under a path you choose.
entries.author: voltius

snippets.name: What is filling the disk
snippets.description: Read-only — it reports, it never deletes.

steps.content:
ROOT={{path}}

df -h -x tmpfs -x devtmpfs
echo
echo "Largest directories under $ROOT:"
sudo du -h -x --max-depth=3 "$ROOT" 2>/dev/null | sort -rh | head -20

entries.name: Install Docker
entries.description: Docker's official convenience script, then the post-install step that lets your user run docker without sudo.
entries.author: voltius

snippets.name: Install Docker Engine
snippets.description: Docker's convenience script. Docker documents it for development, not production — on a production host install from the apt/dnf repository instead.

steps.content:
curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com -o /tmp/get-docker.sh

# Read it before running it — this is the whole point of downloading first.
less /tmp/get-docker.sh

sudo sh /tmp/get-docker.sh
rm -f /tmp/get-docker.sh
sudo docker version

snippets.name: Run docker without sudo
snippets.description: Adds you to the docker group. Note this grants root-equivalent access to the host — that is inherent to the docker group, not to this snippet.

steps.content:
sudo groupadd -f docker
sudo usermod -aG docker "$USER"

echo "Added $USER to the docker group. Log out and back in for it to take effect,"
echo "or run: newgrp docker"

snippets.name: Verify Docker works
snippets.description: Runs hello-world and prints the daemon's disk usage.

steps.content:
docker run --rm hello-world
docker system df

entries.name: Install Node (nvm) + pnpm
entries.description: nvm, the current Node LTS, and pnpm enabled through Corepack.
entries.author: voltius

snippets.name: Install nvm
snippets.description: Pinned to a release tag rather than a branch, so the script you run is the one that was reviewed.

steps.content:
curl -o- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nvm-sh/nvm/v0.40.6/install.sh | bash

# nvm is a shell function, so a new shell (or this) is needed before nvm works.
export NVM_DIR="$HOME/.nvm"
[ -s "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh" ] && . "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh"
nvm --version

snippets.name: Install Node LTS
snippets.description: Installs the current LTS and makes it the default for new shells.

steps.content:
export NVM_DIR="$HOME/.nvm"
[ -s "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh" ] && . "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh"

nvm install --lts
nvm alias default 'lts/*'
node --version
npm --version

snippets.name: Enable pnpm via Corepack
snippets.description: Corepack ships with Node, so pnpm needs no separate installer.

steps.content:
export NVM_DIR="$HOME/.nvm"
[ -s "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh" ] && . "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh"

npm install --global corepack@latest
corepack enable pnpm
pnpm --version

entries.name: Is port {{port}} in use?
entries.description: Shows what is listening on a port, and the process that owns it. Prompts for the port when you run it.
entries.author: voltius

snippets.name: Is port {{port}} in use?
snippets.description: Falls back from ss to lsof to netstat, so it works on a minimal host.

steps.content:
PORT={{port}}

if command -v ss >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  OUT=$(ss -tulpnH "sport = :$PORT" 2>/dev/null)
elif command -v lsof >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  OUT=$(lsof -nP -iTCP:"$PORT" -sTCP:LISTEN 2>/dev/null; lsof -nP -iUDP:"$PORT" 2>/dev/null)
else
  OUT=$(netstat -tulpn 2>/dev/null | grep -E "[:.]$PORT[[:space:]]")
fi

if [ -n "$OUT" ]; then
  echo "Port $PORT is IN USE:"
  echo "$OUT"
else
  echo "Port $PORT is free (nothing listening)."
  echo "Note: without sudo you may not see sockets owned by other users."
fi

entries.name: Install uv
entries.description: Astral's standalone installer for uv, the fast Python package and project manager.
entries.author: voltius

snippets.name: Install uv
snippets.description: No Python needed first — uv ships its own.

steps.content:
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh

# The installer writes to ~/.local/bin and updates your shell profile.
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
uv --version

entries.name: What is listening
entries.description: Every listening TCP and UDP socket with the owning process, sorted by port.
entries.author: voltius

steps.content:
# sudo shows the process for sockets owned by other users; without it those
# rows still appear, just without a name.
if command -v ss >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  sudo ss -tulpn 2>/dev/null || ss -tulpn
else
  sudo netstat -tulpn 2>/dev/null || netstat -tulpn
fi

entries.name: Server triage
entries.description: Why did it die, what is eating the disk that you can safely reclaim, and who has been logging in.
entries.author: voltius

snippets.name: Why did it die
snippets.description: Recent boots, OOM kills, failed services and the tail of the kernel log.

steps.content:
# The three things that explain "it was working yesterday": a reboot, an OOM
# kill, or a service that gave up.
echo "== Uptime and recent boots =="
uptime
command -v last >/dev/null 2>&1 && last reboot 2>/dev/null | head -5

echo
echo "== OOM kills =="
if command -v journalctl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  journalctl -k --no-pager 2>/dev/null | grep -iE "out of memory|oom-kill" | tail -20
elif [ -r /var/log/kern.log ]; then
  grep -iE "out of memory|oom-kill" /var/log/kern.log 2>/dev/null | tail -20
else
  dmesg 2>/dev/null | grep -iE "out of memory|oom-kill" | tail -20
fi
echo "(no lines above means no OOM kill was recorded)"

echo
echo "== Failed services =="
if command -v systemctl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  systemctl --failed --no-pager
elif command -v rc-status >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  rc-status --crashed 2>/dev/null || rc-status 2>/dev/null
else
  echo "no service manager found"
fi

echo
echo "== Last 20 kernel messages =="
OUT=$(dmesg 2>/dev/null | tail -20)
if [ -n "$OUT" ]; then
  echo "$OUT"
else
  echo "dmesg not readable without root"
fi

snippets.name: Reclaim disk safely
snippets.description: Shows the size of the journal, package caches and /tmp, then reclaims only those. Never touches images, volumes or your data.

steps.content:
# Only caches and rotated logs are touched. Images, volumes and your data are
# never in scope here — that is what makes this safe to run on a live box.
echo "== Disk before =="
df -h / | tail -1

echo
echo "== What can be reclaimed =="
[ -d /var/log/journal ] && sudo du -sh /var/log/journal 2>/dev/null
[ -d /var/cache/apt ]   && sudo du -sh /var/cache/apt 2>/dev/null
[ -d /var/cache/dnf ]   && sudo du -sh /var/cache/dnf 2>/dev/null
[ -d /var/cache/apk ]   && sudo du -sh /var/cache/apk 2>/dev/null

echo
# Shown for context only — files here can be in active use, so this script
# never clears /tmp automatically.
echo "== /tmp (shown only — not cleared automatically) =="
sudo du -sh /tmp 2>/dev/null

echo
echo "== Reclaiming =="
command -v journalctl >/dev/null 2>&1 && sudo journalctl --vacuum-time=7d
command -v apt-get    >/dev/null 2>&1 && sudo apt-get clean && echo "apt cache cleaned"
command -v dnf        >/dev/null 2>&1 && sudo dnf clean all
command -v apk        >/dev/null 2>&1 && sudo rm -rf /var/cache/apk/* && echo "apk cache cleaned"

echo
echo "== Disk after =="
df -h / | tail -1

snippets.name: Who logged in
snippets.description: Current sessions, recent logins and failed attempts, from whichever of wtmp, btmp or the journal this host keeps.

steps.content:
# Who has had access recently, and who tried and failed — the first two
# questions after a lockout scare or a suspected intrusion.
echo "== Connected right now =="
who 2>/dev/null || w 2>/dev/null || echo "no utmp on this host"

echo
echo "== Last 15 logins =="
OUT=$(last -n 15 2>/dev/null | head -16)
if [ -n "$OUT" ]; then
  echo "$OUT"
else
  echo "no wtmp on this host"
fi

echo
echo "== Failed attempts =="
if command -v lastb >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  OUT=$(sudo lastb -n 15 2>/dev/null | head -16)
  if [ -n "$OUT" ]; then
    echo "$OUT"
  else
    echo "no btmp on this host"
  fi
elif command -v journalctl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  OUT=$(sudo journalctl -u ssh -u sshd --no-pager 2>/dev/null | grep -i "failed password" | tail -15)
  if [ -n "$OUT" ]; then
    echo "$OUT"
  else
    echo "no failed-password entries found"
  fi
elif [ -r /var/log/auth.log ]; then
  OUT=$(sudo grep -i "failed password" /var/log/auth.log 2>/dev/null | tail -15)
  if [ -n "$OUT" ]; then
    echo "$OUT"
  else
    echo "no failed-password entries found"
  fi
else
  echo "no auth log available"
fi

entries.name: Persistent sessions (tmux/screen)
entries.description: Make your SSH sessions survive a dropped connection, check whether a host already does, and clean up the ones you left behind.
entries.author: voltius

snippets.name: Install tmux
snippets.description: Installs tmux with whichever package manager this host has. Clears the "session will not survive disconnects" warning.

steps.content:
# Voltius wraps an SSH session in tmux (or screen) so it survives a dropped
# connection. With neither installed the session dies with the link, which is
# what the "tmux/screen not found" banner is telling you.
if command -v tmux >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "tmux is already installed"
else
  if   command -v apt-get >/dev/null 2>&1; then sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y tmux
  elif command -v dnf     >/dev/null 2>&1; then sudo dnf install -y tmux
  elif command -v apk     >/dev/null 2>&1; then sudo apk add --no-cache tmux
  elif command -v pacman  >/dev/null 2>&1; then sudo pacman -S --noconfirm tmux
  else echo "no supported package manager found"; fi
fi
tmux -V

snippets.name: Will this host keep my session alive?
snippets.description: Reports which multiplexer is installed, lists the sessions already running, and says what that means for a dropped connection.

steps.content:
# Voltius prefers tmux, falls back to screen, and warns when neither exists.
screen_ls() {
  if command -v screen >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    SCR_OUT=$(screen -ls 2>/dev/null)
    SCR_RC=$?
    if [ "$SCR_RC" -eq 0 ] && [ -n "$SCR_OUT" ]; then
      printf '%s\n' "$SCR_OUT"
    else
      echo "screen: no sessions"
    fi
  fi
}

for m in tmux screen; do
  if command -v "$m" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    case "$m" in
      tmux)   VER=$(tmux -V 2>&1 | head -1) ;;
      screen) VER=$(screen -v 2>&1 | head -1) ;;
    esac
    if [ -n "$VER" ]; then
      echo "$m: $VER"
    else
      echo "$m: installed (version not reported)"
    fi
  else
    echo "$m: not installed"
  fi
done

echo
echo "== Sessions on this host =="
command -v tmux >/dev/null 2>&1 && { tmux ls 2>/dev/null || echo "tmux: no sessions"; }
screen_ls

echo
if command -v tmux >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "=> Your session survives a dropped connection (tmux)."
elif command -v screen >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "=> Your session survives a dropped connection (screen)."
else
  echo "=> Nothing persistent here: a dropped connection kills the session."
  echo "   Install tmux to fix that."
fi

snippets.name: Kill a stale session
snippets.description: Lists your sessions, kills the one you name, then lists them again. A name that does not exist kills nothing.

steps.content:
# The list is printed before anything is killed, on purpose — kill the wrong
# session and you lose whatever was running inside it. Both kills below only
# fire on an exact name match: tmux and screen both do prefix matching by
# default, so an unanchored match could kill session "foobar" when you asked
# to kill "foo".
TARGET="{{session}}"

screen_ls() {
  if command -v screen >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    SCR_OUT=$(screen -ls 2>/dev/null)
    SCR_RC=$?
    if [ "$SCR_RC" -eq 0 ] && [ -n "$SCR_OUT" ]; then
      printf '%s\n' "$SCR_OUT"
    else
      echo "screen: no sessions"
    fi
  fi
}

# Exact-match check for screen: screen -S/-X quit prefix-matches like tmux
# does, and unlike tmux there is no "=name" anchor to force an exact match,
# so we parse `screen -ls` ourselves and only proceed on an exact hit.
screen_has_exact() {
  command -v screen >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
  SCR_OUT=$(screen -ls 2>/dev/null)
  SCR_RC=$?
  [ "$SCR_RC" -eq 0 ] && [ -n "$SCR_OUT" ] || return 1
  printf '%s\n' "$SCR_OUT" | awk -F'\t' -v t="$1" '
    NF >= 2 { id = $2; sub(/^[0-9]+\./, "", id); if (id == t) { found = 1; exit } }
    END { exit !found }
  '
}

echo "== Sessions before =="
command -v tmux >/dev/null 2>&1 && { tmux ls 2>/dev/null || echo "tmux: no sessions"; }
screen_ls

echo
echo "== Killing '$TARGET' =="
if tmux kill-session -t "=$TARGET" 2>/dev/null; then
  echo "killed tmux session $TARGET"
elif screen_has_exact "$TARGET" && screen -S "$TARGET" -X quit 2>/dev/null; then
  echo "killed screen session $TARGET"
else
  echo "no session named '$TARGET' — nothing killed"
fi

echo
echo "== Sessions after =="
command -v tmux >/dev/null 2>&1 && { tmux ls 2>/dev/null || echo "tmux: no sessions"; }
screen_ls

entries.name: Service ops
entries.description: Inspect, restart and follow a service, on systemd, OpenRC or plain SysV alike.
entries.author: voltius

snippets.name: Inspect a service
snippets.description: Status plus the last log lines, from whichever service manager and log source this host has.

steps.content:
SVC="{{service}}"
LINES="{{lines:number:20}}"

if command -v systemctl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  systemctl status "$SVC" --no-pager
  echo
  echo "== last $LINES log lines =="
  LOG=$(journalctl -u "$SVC" -n "$LINES" --no-pager 2>&1)
  if [ -n "$LOG" ]; then echo "$LOG"; else echo "no journal entries for $SVC"; fi
elif command -v rc-service >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  rc-service "$SVC" status
  echo
  echo "== last $LINES log lines =="
  tail -n "$LINES" "/var/log/$SVC.log" 2>/dev/null || echo "no /var/log/$SVC.log on this host"
elif command -v service >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  service "$SVC" status
  echo
  echo "== last $LINES log lines =="
  tail -n "$LINES" "/var/log/$SVC.log" 2>/dev/null || echo "no /var/log/$SVC.log on this host"
else
  echo "no service manager found (systemctl, rc-service, service)"
fi

snippets.name: Restart a service
snippets.description: Shows the state, restarts, then shows it again so you can see whether it actually came back.

steps.content:
SVC="{{service}}"

# State before and after, either side of the restart — a restart you cannot see
# the result of is not worth running.
echo "== Before =="
if command -v systemctl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  STATE=$(systemctl is-active "$SVC" 2>&1)
elif command -v rc-service >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  STATE=$(rc-service "$SVC" status 2>&1)
elif command -v service >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  STATE=$(service "$SVC" status 2>&1)
else
  STATE=""
fi
if [ -n "$STATE" ]; then echo "$STATE"; else echo "unknown"; fi

echo
echo "== Restarting $SVC =="
if   command -v systemctl  >/dev/null 2>&1; then sudo systemctl restart "$SVC"
elif command -v rc-service >/dev/null 2>&1; then sudo rc-service "$SVC" restart
elif command -v service    >/dev/null 2>&1; then sudo service "$SVC" restart
else echo "no service manager found"; fi

echo
echo "== After =="
if command -v systemctl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  systemctl status "$SVC" --no-pager 2>/dev/null | head -12
elif command -v rc-service >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  STATE=$(rc-service "$SVC" status 2>&1)
  if [ -n "$STATE" ]; then echo "$STATE"; else echo "unknown"; fi
elif command -v service >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  STATE=$(service "$SVC" status 2>&1)
  if [ -n "$STATE" ]; then echo "$STATE"; else echo "unknown"; fi
else
  echo "unknown"
fi

snippets.name: Follow a service's logs
snippets.description: Live tail of a service's logs. Runs until you press Ctrl-C.

steps.content:
SVC="{{service}}"

# Runs until you stop it: press Ctrl-C in the terminal to stop following.
if command -v journalctl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  journalctl -u "$SVC" -f -n 50
elif [ -r "/var/log/$SVC.log" ]; then
  tail -f -n 50 "/var/log/$SVC.log"
elif [ -r /var/log/messages ]; then
  tail -f -n 50 /var/log/messages | grep --line-buffered -i "$SVC"
else
  echo "no log source found for $SVC (tried journalctl, /var/log/$SVC.log, /var/log/messages)"
fi

entries.name: Install gdu
entries.description: An interactive disk usage browser — walk the tree instead of reading a list.
entries.author: voltius

snippets.name: Install gdu
snippets.description: Uses the distro package where there is one, otherwise the official release binary into ~/.local/bin.

steps.content:
# gdu is an interactive disk usage browser — the one to reach for when you want
# to walk the tree instead of reading a list.
# A prior run may have landed gdu in ~/.local/bin, which is not on PATH for a
# non-interactive shell (e.g. `ssh host sh -s < script`) — put it there so the
# already-installed check below actually finds it.
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"

if command -v gdu >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "gdu is already installed"
else
  # Only some distros package it; Debian/Ubuntu generally do not, so those fall
  # through to the release binary below.
  if   command -v apk    >/dev/null 2>&1; then sudo apk add --no-cache gdu 2>/dev/null
  elif command -v pacman >/dev/null 2>&1; then sudo pacman -S --noconfirm gdu 2>/dev/null
  elif command -v dnf    >/dev/null 2>&1; then sudo dnf install -y gdu 2>/dev/null
  fi
fi

if ! command -v gdu >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  case "$(uname -m)" in
    x86_64|amd64)  ARCH=amd64 ;;
    aarch64|arm64) ARCH=arm64 ;;
    *) echo "unsupported architecture: $(uname -m)"; exit 1 ;;
  esac
  mkdir -p "$HOME/.local/bin"
  curl -fsSL "https://github.com/dundee/gdu/releases/latest/download/gdu_linux_${ARCH}.tgz" | tar xz -C /tmp
  mv "/tmp/gdu_linux_${ARCH}" "$HOME/.local/bin/gdu"
  chmod +x "$HOME/.local/bin/gdu"
  # The installer wrote to ~/.local/bin; this shell may not have it on PATH yet.
  export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
fi

gdu --version | head -1

entries.name: Update all packages
entries.description: Prints what would be upgraded, then upgrades it. Works on apt, dnf, apk and pacman.
entries.author: voltius

snippets.name: Update all packages
snippets.description: The upgrade list comes first, so nothing changes before you have seen it.

steps.content:
# The upgrade list is printed first so you can stop before it runs if something
# on it surprises you.
echo "== What would change =="
if command -v apt-get >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  if sudo apt-get update >/dev/null; then
    OUT=$(apt list --upgradable 2>/dev/null | tail -n +2)
    if [ -n "$OUT" ]; then echo "$OUT"; else echo "up to date — nothing to upgrade"; fi
  else
    echo "(could not refresh the package index — skipping the preview)"
  fi
elif command -v dnf >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  dnf check-update || true
elif command -v apk >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  if sudo apk update >/dev/null; then
    OUT=$(apk list --upgradable 2>/dev/null)
    if [ -n "$OUT" ]; then echo "$OUT"; else echo "up to date — nothing to upgrade"; fi
  else
    echo "(could not refresh the package index — skipping the preview)"
  fi
elif command -v pacman >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  if pacman -Sy >/dev/null; then
    OUT=$(pacman -Qu)
    if [ -n "$OUT" ]; then echo "$OUT"; else echo "up to date — nothing to upgrade"; fi
  else
    echo "(could not refresh the package index — skipping the preview)"
  fi
else
  echo "no supported package manager found"
fi

echo
echo "== Upgrading =="
if   command -v apt-get >/dev/null 2>&1; then sudo apt-get upgrade -y
elif command -v dnf     >/dev/null 2>&1; then sudo dnf upgrade -y
elif command -v apk     >/dev/null 2>&1; then sudo apk upgrade
elif command -v pacman  >/dev/null 2>&1; then sudo pacman -Su --noconfirm
fi

echo
echo "== Done =="

entries.name: Firewall status
entries.description: What this host is actually filtering, via ufw, firewalld, nftables or iptables.
entries.author: voltius

snippets.name: Firewall status
snippets.description: Read-only: reports the active ruleset and changes nothing.

steps.content:
# Read-only: reports the rules, changes nothing.
if command -v ufw >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  sudo ufw status verbose
elif command -v firewall-cmd >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  sudo firewall-cmd --list-all
elif command -v nft >/dev/null 2>&1 && sudo nft list ruleset 2>/dev/null | grep -q .; then
  sudo nft list ruleset
elif command -v iptables >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  sudo iptables -L -n -v
else
  echo "no firewall tool found (ufw, firewalld, nftables, iptables)"
fi
